body:
Engine-internal memory writes: bypass the mixin stack when safe
----------------------------------------------------------------

When the Rust engine's SimProcedure bounce replays dirty pages back into
a live Python ``SimState`` (``RustStateSyncMixin`` in
``angr/exploration/rust_state_sync.py``), routing every byte through
``state.memory.store`` pays the full memory-mixin stack even though the
write is already engine-internal and already passes
``inspect=False``/``disable_actions=True``. Measured on the
``sc_memreplay`` bottleneck (angr-gorvf.10): naive replay cost 325 ms per
crossing, of which only 13 ms was the FFI page fetch. The rest was the
Python-side store — roughly 260 ms from ~169 symbolic objects per page
routed through the generic memory-mixin stack at ~32 us/object, plus
~6.5 ms from ``UltraPage.store``'s quadratic byte-at-a-time concrete-store
loop for a single 4096-byte page (an upstream angr perf bug, still live
in ``angr/storage/memory_mixins/paged_memory/pages/ultra_page.py``).

**Fix pattern** (``_acquire_ultrapage`` + ``_blit_concrete_page`` in
``RustStateSyncMixin``): acquire the destination page once via
``memory._get_page(pageno, writing=True)`` — ``writing=True`` still
routes through ``acquire_unique()`` so copy-on-write correctness is
preserved; never touch ``state.memory._pages`` directly — then:

1. Blit concrete bytes as a single bytearray slice assignment and zero
   the ``symbolic_bitmap`` over the range (mirrors ``UltraPage.store``'s
   own concrete branch, which also leaves ``symbolic_data`` alone since
   loads consult the bitmap).
2. Store symbolic entries via ``page.store(offset, ast, size, endness,
   memory=..., page_addr=..., cooperate=False)``, which runs the same
   decomposition the mixin would have.

Result on ``csaw_wyvern``: 10.8 ms → 2.7 ms per crossing (-75%).

**Generalizable rule:** any engine-internal ``SimState`` memory write
that is already passing ``inspect=False``/``disable_actions=True`` is a
candidate for this page-acquire-and-blit bypass. The only store-side
memory mixin with real state is ``ConvenientMappingsMixin``, and it is
inert (so safely skippable) unless ``MEMORY_SYMBOLIC_BYTES_MAP`` /
``REVERSE_MEMORY_NAME_MAP`` / ``REVERSE_MEMORY_HASH_MAP`` is set — check
for those before applying the bypass elsewhere.
